reason: Portable zip, free, so I'd grab it and throw some PSD and alpha PNGs at it. But one dev at 0.4 with a gallery, editor and batch tools bolted on is not the 'just show the picture' tool I want, and I won't rebuild my habits around something that may be abandoned next year.
why_switch_or_not: The speed numbers and the PSD/AI/alpha support are what would get me to try it, and having one app instead of juggling Honeyview, VLC and a RAW tool is a real draw. I would not make it default because I don't know if it still gets updates in 12 months, and I don't need an editor, importer or batch rename inside a viewer. My 200,000-picture drive is the real test, and nothing here tells me how the gallery copes with that many files.
current_app_pros: Honeyview opens comics and archives instantly and does nothing else. VLC/MPC-HC handle video without fuss. Blender and RawTherapee/darktable do their jobs properly. Each one is boring and predictable, and none of them will vanish on me.
current_app_pains: Having a different app for each file type is annoying, and PSD and alpha PNG previews are the weak spot in the whole setup. The pain is mild, though. It all works and I know where everything is.
objection: One developer, version 0.4: will it still be maintained next year? And it looks like it does a lot more than viewing, which is the opposite of what I want.
would_change_my_mind: A year or more of steady releases (or a public roadmap and open source), plus a way to turn off the gallery/editor/importer so it is only a viewer, plus proof it stays smooth browsing a 200k-file folder tree.
